title: Symplectic Barnes-Wall GKP Codes: Deterministic $O(N \log^2 N)$ Decoding and Logarithmic Rate Scaling
abstract: We construct an explicit symplectic realization of the Barnes-Wall lattice that yields a family of multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes with encoding rate $R = \frac{1}{2}\log_2 N$ and a deterministic $O(N\log^2 N)$ bounded-distance decoder. The recursive generator $G_{m+1} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} G_m & 0 \\ G_m & R_m G_m \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ with $R_m = I + Ω$ simultaneously guarantees symplectic integrality for valid quantum stabilizers and preserves the exact Barnes-Wall decoding structure through a chain of isometric isomorphisms. The code distance is constant at $Δ^2 = 1$ (in units of $2π$), representing an explicit distance--rate tradeoff in which logarithmic encoding efficiency is achieved at the cost of non-scaling protection. This construction provides a deterministic, space-efficient paradigm for GKP error correction in platforms supporting non-local modular connectivity.
summary: This paper introduces symplectic Barnes-Wall GKP codes that achieve an optimal logarithmic encoding rate ($R \propto \log N$) while maintaining a constant error protection distance ($\Delta^2=1$). By utilizing the structure of the Barnes-Wall lattice, they provide a deterministic and efficient decoding scheme for continuous-variable quantum error correction.
main_problem: Designing practical, high-dimensional Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes for quantum error correction in continuous-variable systems while overcoming the limitations of rate-distance trade-offs.
main_result: The authors construct an explicit family of GKP codes based on the Barnes-Wall lattice achieving a logarithmic encoding rate ($R =  rac{1}{2}\log_2 N$) with a constant code distance ($\Delta^2=1$).
method: They use a recursive generator structure to realize a symplectic embedding of the Barnes-Wall lattice, enabling a deterministic $O(N\log^2 N)$ decoder.
model_or_system: The system involves continuous-variable (CV) bosonic modes encoded into GKP states defined by lattices $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^{2N}$. The construction leverages the symplectic structure and global entanglement properties of the Barnes-Wall lattice.
key_observables: Encoding Rate ($R =  rac{1}{2}\log_2 N$), Code Distance ($\Delta^2=1$), Decoding Complexity ($O(N\log^2 N)$).
important_parameters: The constant distance $\Delta^2=1$ represents a specific, non-scaling protection level achieved at the expense of rate scaling.
main_assumptions: The construction requires hardware supporting non-local modular connectivity to implement the global syndrome extraction and decoding process.
figures_summary: Figures compare code families (e.g., Surface-GKP vs SBW-GKP) showing superior rate scaling for the proposed method, and illustrate the operational cycle involving global entanglement.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by reviewing limitations of existing codes, introduces the symplectic realization of the Barnes-Wall lattice via a recursive generator, proves the resulting code parameters (rate and distance), and details the transformation of the decoding problem from the dual lattice to the primal lattice for efficient computation.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, high-performance theoretical blueprint for fault-tolerant quantum computing using CV systems, directly impacting hardware requirements for photonic or superconducting implementations.
